brief: The FOMC hiked 25bps to an upper bound of 4.00% unanimously, the first hike since 2023, which Natixis calls the path of least resistance after a higher-than-expected August inflation print. The bank argues the move does little to fix inflation but buys time to see if that print was a bump or something worse. Being cautiously optimistic on the inflation trajectory, Natixis flags a possible one-off hike, but because consistently encouraging prints are hard to string together, its base case pencils in another hike in December followed by an extended hold through 2027. August retail sales rebounded broadly (1.2% m/m headline and ex-autos/gas, control group 1.4% versus 0.5% consensus, real spending up 0.84% m/m), reinforcing that consumer spending is firm and giving the Fed room to keep tightening. Separately, the EU proposed a largely symbolic associate-membership status for Canada after new US tariffs on Canadian goods, prompting a Trump threat of tariffs against Europe. Brazil's BCB rate-cut pace is tied to fiscal-adjustment credibility (7-9% terminal rate if robust, 10-12% if shallow), while Banxico is expected to hold at 6.50%, resisting mechanical tracking of Fed hikes unless MXN depreciation turns disorderly.
